This is an open continuous announcement to fill current and future vacancies, until 07/30/2026. This is an open continuous announcement with cutoff dates.

Applications will be referred based on receipt of application and established cutoff dates as follows: 1st cutoff date: 07/17/2026 Last cutoff date: 07/24/2026 We encourage you to read this entire vacancy announcement prior to submitting your application. This position is eligible for Remote/Virtual work.

However, this position may fall under the Presidential Memorandum titled "Return to In-Person Work" which will require you to go into the office if you are located within 50 miles of a Department of Education facility in these locations: Washington, DC, Dallas, TX, San Francisco, CA, Seattle, WA, Kansas City, MO, Chicago, Il, Atlanta, GA, Philadelphia, PA, New York City, NY, and location is negotiable.

Actual salary will be based on location of selectee. Locality pay tables available at www.opm.gov . As a IT Project Manager, GS-2210-14, you will be responsible for:
· Managing and ensuring the performance of role-specific tasks: project, time, resource, and budget management, scope management, schedule management, risk management and coordination on contracts and contracts management and oversight.
· Managing the identification and coordination of technical activities of project team(s), prioritizes and facilitates technical tasks and sequence tracks of work, of IT projects/initiatives in an iterative, incremental, parallel, and time-boxed manner aligned to deliver business value.
· Managing and ensures the performance of role-specific tasks: project, time, resource, and budget management, scope management, schedule management, risk management and coordination on contracts and contracts management and oversight (in role as Contracting Officer's Technical Representative [COTR]/ Contracting Office Representative [COR]).
· Identifying and consulting on technical resource requirements for projects (e.g., analysts, developers, quality assurance), and onboard qualified resources to support project needs.
· Managing effectively and efficiently various Information Technology (IT) projects.
Minimum Qualification Requirements You may meet the minimum qualifications for the GS-14, if you possess the specialized experience.

Specialized Experience for the GS-14 One year of experience in either federal or non-federal service that is equivalent to at least a GS-13 performing two (2) out of three (3) of the following duties or work assignments: 1.

Experience leading cross-functional project teams utilizing agile methodologies and practices while identifying and managing associated risks, issues, contracts, and change requests to meet schedule, budget, and organizational policies and objectives to facilitate the delivery of incremental software or system enhancements. 2.

Experience in applying agile methods to support technical integration, system modernization, and continuous improvement initiatives to ensure IT systems are compatible with architecture, cloud platforms, system interfaces, and cybersecurity requirements to reduce technical debt and improve release predictability. 3.

Experience implementing risk and issue management processes, ensuring potential blockers are identified early, escalated appropriately, resolved and aligned with established change-control processes within agile release frameworks to adhere to program timelines and deliverables.

Basic Experience Requirements You must possess IT related experience (paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training (e.g., IT certification), as appropriate) demonstrating each of the nine competencies listed below. 1. Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. 2.

Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. 3.

Decision Making - Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change. 4.

Information Management - Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems. 5.

Interpersonal Skills - Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations 6.

Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. 7.

Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. 8. Teamwork - Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals. 9.

Technical Competence – Uses knowledge that is acquired through formal training or on-the-job experience to perform one's job; works with, understands, and evaluates technical information related to the job; advises others on technical issues.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs) The quality of your experience will be measured by the extent to which you possess the following knowledge, skills and abilities (KSAs).

You do not need to provide separate narrative responses to these KSAs, as they will be measured by your responses to the occupational questionnaire (you may preview the occupational questionnaire by clicking the link at the end of the Evaluations section of this vacancy announcement). 1.

Skill in leading and directing people, teams and programs / projects associated with IT application development; the development of mission-critical enterprise class applications, and enterprise-wide IT projects 2.

Ability to deliver mission critical IT initiatives to meet organizational objectives using agile project management tools or techniques. 3. Ability to develop acquisition artifacts required to procure, and provide services for implementation, and operations and maintenance of an IT system and oversee vendor performance upon contract award. 4.

Ability to lead complex IT initiatives while managing changing priorities, evolving legislative or regulatory requirements and coordinating with various internal and external stakeholders.

This position will serve as a Behavioral Health Interdisciplinary Program (BHIP) Program Manager at the Mosley CBOC in Aurora, Colorado.

As a BHIP Program Manager, the Psychologist assists in planning, establishing, and implementing policies and procedures, developing individual or group goals and objectives, as well as monitoring, operating, evaluating, coordinating, and overseeing the multidisciplinary staff of their assigned BHIP team(s).

Provides program management and oversight of interdisciplinary BHIP team(s). Maintains administrative supervisory responsibility of all direct reports and Team Lead responsibility of all other members of their BHIP team(s).

Oversees the implementation of BHIP services, including ensuring that appropriate processes/procedures are followed, Veteran care needs are addressed, and Veteran complaints are addressed.

Identifies procedural issues related to BHIP treatment and care coordination and works toward process improvement in coordination with the other BHIP Program Coordinators, Program Managers and the Section Chief.

Ensures the multidisciplinary staff under their supervision are aware of and adhere to all current directives and handbooks of the Veterans Affairs Administration, meet current applicable Joint Commission standards, state licensure standards, and VA-OIG oversight requirements.

Oversees and/or ensures that appropriate processes are identified and followed related to BHIP sub-programs, such as psychological testing and groups. Develops and maintains high-quality team functioning and processes while meeting all Environment of Care and programmatic requirements.

Works closely with the Primary Mental Health Section Chief, Mental Health Service leadership, other Mental Health program leadership, and other services through the VA Eastern Colorado Health Care System. Fosters a cohesive interdisciplinary team environment.

Oversees quality control issues and performance measures in collaboration with the Primary Mental Health Section Chief and throughout VA ECHCS. Assists the Section Chief in overseeing compliance with the successful execution of Mental Health Performance Measures, SAIL, workload, VERA capture, Veteran patient satisfaction, and quality assurance.

Utilizes the service recovery model with Veteran patients who express dissatisfaction or concerns regarding their mental health care as requested; provides consultation for all mental health clinicians regarding the clinical care of complex cases.

Provides overarching supervision, including annual performance ratings, for direct report employees, including Psychologists, Social Workers, and Licensed Professional Mental Health Counselors (LPMHC).

Provides Team Lead oversight of all members of the BHIP team(s), including non-direct report staff, such as Psychiatrists, Nurse Practitioners, Physician Assistants, Clinical Pharmacists, Nurses, and Peer Support Specialists.

Clearly communicates established guidelines and performance expectations for staff through the formal employee performance management system. Develops functional statements and performance standards. Observes workers' performance, demonstrates and conducts work performance critiques.

Provides informal feedback and periodically evaluates employee performance. Identifies training needs of employees and arranges training as appropriate. Works to resolve informal complaints and grievances; develops work improvement plans recommending personnel actions as necessary.

Conducts individual, group, and couples therapy and psychological assessment for Veterans engaged in BHIP. Work Schedule: Monday-Friday 8 AM - 4:30 PM Virtual: This is not a virtual position.

Applicants pending the completion of educational or certification/licensure requirements may be referred and tentatively selected but may not be hired until all requirements are met.

Basic Requirements: Education: Have a doctoral degree in psychology from a graduate program in psychology accredited by the American Psychological Association (APA), the Psychological Clinical Science Accreditation System (PCSAS), or the Canadian Psychological Association (CPA) at the time the program was completed.

The specialty area of the degree must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed. For the purpose of meeting this requirement, the term "specialty area" refers to the specific specialty areas recognized by the accrediting body and not to specific job duties that might require special skills.

Currently, APA accredits doctoral programs in the specialty areas of clinical psychology, counseling psychology, school psychology, or combinations of two or more of those areas. PCSAS accredits doctoral programs in psychological clinical science.

CPA accredits doctoral programs in clinical psychology, counseling psychology, clinical neuropsychology, and school psychology. There are no job assignments in VHA that require the skills of a school psychologist; therefore, an applicant with a degree in the specialty area of school psychology is not eligible for appointment.

Strictly for the purpose of determining eligibility for appointment as a psychologist in VHA, there is no distinction between the specialty areas (with the exception of school psychology).

OR Have a doctoral degree in any area of psychology and, in addition, successfully complete a re- specialization program (including documentation of an approved internship completed as part of the re- specialization program) meeting both of the following conditions: The re-specialization program must be completed in an APA or a CPA accredited doctoral program; and, the specialty in which the applicant is retrained must be consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

OR Have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally-accredited institution, with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature.] AND Internships Have successfully completed a professional psychology internship training program that was accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed and that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed OR New VHA psychology internship programs that are in the process of applying for APA accreditation are acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement, provided that such programs were sanctioned by the VHA Central Office Program Director for Psychology and the VHA Office of Academic Affiliations at the time that the individual was an intern; OR VHA facilities that offered full-time, one-year pre-doctoral internships prior to PL 96- 151 (pre- 1979) are considered to be acceptable in fulfillment of the internship requirement; OR Applicants who completed an internship that was not accredited by APA or CPA at the time the program was completed may be considered eligible for hire only if they are currently board certified by the American Board of Professional Psychology in a specialty area that is consistent with the assignment for which the applicant is to be employed.

(NOTE: Once board certified, the employee is required to maintain board certification.) OR Applicants who have a doctoral degree awarded between 1951 and 1978 from a regionally- accredited institution with a dissertation primarily psychological in nature may fulfill this internship requirement by having the equivalent of a one-year supervised internship experience in a site specifically acceptable to the candidate's doctoral program.

If the internship experience is not noted on the applicant's official transcript, the applicant must provide a statement from the doctoral program verifying that the equivalent of a one- year supervised internship experience was completed in a site acceptable to the doctoral program.

Licensure: Hold a full, current, and unrestricted license to practice psychology at the doctoral level in a State, Territory, or Commonwealth of the United States, or the District of Columbia. Exception.

Non-licensed applicants who otherwise meet the eligibility requirements may be given a temporary appointment as a "graduate psychologist" at the GS-11 or GS- 12 grade under the authority of 38 U.S.C. § 7405 [(c)(2)(B)] for a period not to exceed two years from the date of employment on the condition that such a psychologist provide care only under the supervision of a psychologist who is licensed.

Failure to obtain licensure during that period is justification for termination of the temporary appointment. Grade Determinations: Psychology Program Manager, GS-14 Experience: At least three years of experience as a professional psychologist, with at least one year equivalent to the GS-13 grade level.

Demonstrated Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: In addition to the experience above, the candidate must demonstrate all of the following KSAs: Ability to organize work, set priorities, delegate tasks, and meet multiple deadlines.

Knowledge of and ability to utilize evidence based practices and clinical practice guidelines appropriately and ability to guide staff in using these tools. Ability to deal effectively with individuals or groups. Skill in managing and directing the work of others to accomplish program goals and objectives.

Ability to translate management goals and objectives into well-coordinated and controlled work operations. Ability to establish and monitor production and performance priorities and standards. Ability to analyze organizational and operational problems and to develop and implement solutions that result in sound operation of the program.

Preferred Experience: Experience providing outpatient mental health treatment through BHIP, Mental Health/BHIP supervisory experience, Clinical experience providing evidence based psychotherapy. Reference: For more information on this qualification standard, please visit https://www.va.gov/ohrm/QualificationStandards/.

The full performance level of this vacancy is GS-14. The actual grade at which an applicant may be selected for this vacancy is GS-14 Physical Requirements: Physical demands of the work are generally minor, as the position requires sitting, standing, and walking.

The emotional demands can be stressful in working with high-risk for suicide veteran population and their families. A high level of self-awareness is essential. Work is primarily sedentary. May require prolonged standing, moderate walking, and manual dexterity. Requires carrying light items, such as books, files, or laptop computer.

As a your typical work assignments may include: Providing the delegated authority, leadership, management and strategic vision necessary to ensure that the division has the proper agency policies, procedures, and systems in place. Providing administrative and financial support to complete the agency's mission.

Managing all business operations program activities, may include general services functions or financial and procurement functions. Facilitating the development of short and long-range business operations program plans to support the agency goals and objectives. Coordinating with internal and external organizations and headquarters.
For more information on eligibility requirements see: DEA Employment Eligibility Applicants must meet the required qualification requirements described below by the closing date of the announcement. Applicants applying for the GS-15 must meet one of the following requirements: A.

Have at least one full year of specialized experience that is at least equivalent to work performed at the GS-14 grade level.

Specialized experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Qualifying experience must demonstrate the following: 1) Managing the operations programs related to policies, procedures, and systems supporting administrative and financial organization's objectives; 2) Providing administrative and financial support to complete the agency's mission 3) Managing business operations program activities, may include general services functions or financial and procurement functions 4) Facilitating the development of short and long-range business operations program plans to support the agency goals and objectives 5) Coordinating with internal and external organizations and headquarters Additional information on the position qualification requirements are located in the Office of Personnel Management's (OPM) Qualifications Standards Handbook.

Time-In-Grade Requirement: Applicants must meet time-in-grade and time after competitive appointment requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

Professional fields of study and expertise must be pertinent to the park's resources and themes and may include, but are not limited to, history, historic preservation, historical architecture, cultural landscape architecture, archeology, cultural anthropology, museum management, ecology, botany, wildlife management, hydrology, and physical sciences.

Experience may include research, field investigations, laboratory analysis, library research, interpretation or consultative work, preparation of reports for publication, curation and exhibition of collections, or development and implementation of programs and projects which carry out such work.

Experience requires knowledge of professional scientific natural and cultural resources management principles, theories, concepts, methods, and techniques. You must include hours per week worked.

Volunteer Experience: Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Incumbent applies a comprehensive technical knowledge of IT principles, concepts, methods, standards, and practices to: develop and interpret policies, procedures, and strategies governing the planning and delivery of services throughout the agency; provide expert technical advice, guidance, and recommendations to management and other technical specialists on significant IT issues; apply new developments to previously unsolvable problems; and make recommendations that significantly influence important agency IT policies or programs.

Applies a comprehensive technical knowledge of the agency's IT architecture; new IT developments and applications; IT security concepts, standards, and methods; and oral and written communication techniques to: ensure the integration of IT projects and services; develop solutions to integration/interoperability issues; manage projects that meet current and future business requirements and apply and extend, enhance, or optimize the existing architecture; communicate complex technical requirements to non-technical personnel; and prepare briefings for senior management officials on complex/controversial issues.

Incumbent applies a comprehensive technical knowledge in the application of the business value of information; methods and approaches for sharing information through the use of IT assets; capital planning regulations and policies, as applied to the agency's business requirements, performance measurement tools and methods for identifying and resolving IT workforce issues to: develop knowledge management program plans, policies and standards; provide input to the IT capital planning process, and develop, implement, and interpret metrics for the evaluation of IT project effectiveness and efficiency; and leverage resources in the accomplishment of mission requirements.

Incumbent applies a comprehensive technical knowledge in Configuration Management principles and methods for planning or managing the implementation, update, or integration of IT systems components.

Applies a comprehensive technical knowledge of Data Management principles, procedures, and tools of data management, such as modeling techniques, data backup, data recovery, data dictionaries, data warehousing, data mining, data disposal, and data standardization processes.

Applies a comprehensive technical knowledge of Systems Life Cycle management concepts used to plan, develop, implement, operate, and maintain IT systems.

Applies a comprehensive knowledge of IT Systems/Network Security methods, tools, and procedures, including development of information security plans, to prevent IT systems vulnerabilities, and provide or restore security of IT systems and network services.

Applies a comprehensive knowledge of Systems Integration principles, methods, and procedures for installing, integrating, and optimizing IT systems components.

Applies a comprehensive knowledge of Information Technology Architecture methodologies used in the design and development of IT systems, including the physical structure of a system's internal operations and interactions with other systems.

Performs other duties as assigned.

Specialized experience is experience that has equipped you with the particular knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform successfully the duties of the position.

Quello che puoi mettere in movimento.
* Conduci progetti complessi nell'ambito della manutenzione e ammodernamento delle nostre flotte definendo le attività di implementazione, gli obiettivi operativi ed economici.
* Definisci i processi, prepari la documentazione e formi i collaboratori coinvolti.
* Sei responsabile della definizione e creazione della Supply Chain, con particolare attenzione alla Standardizzazione, all'ottimizzazione dei processi, mantenendo i tempi e i costi di produzione definiti, seguendo la strategia aziendale e con una visione end-to-end.
* Le soluzioni, i metodi identificati e implementati devono essere sostenibili in tutti gli ambiti utilizzando le Best Practices di FFS; applicando l'eliminazione degli sprechi usando le tecniche Lean tra le quali il 5S.
* Sei la persona di riferimento in tutti gli ambiti aziendali fino a conclusione della fase di industrializzazione, sorvegli, monitori e intraprendi le misure necessarie per mantenere i costi, qualità e i tempi definiti a completa soddisfazione del cliente e allestendo i report necessari per gli stakeholder.
* Infine gestisci i rischi, anticipando i problemi con le misure adeguate.
Quello che porti con te.
* Sei una persona dinamica, organizzata, precisa, propositiva con buone capacità comunicative, di collaborazione e di negoziazione, responsabile e con doti di Leadership.
* Abilità nelle tecniche Lean di Standardizzazione e Problem Solving, atti a risolvere e anticipare i problemi, con spiccate doti nell'identificare delle vere cause dei problemi e nell'identificare le opportunità.
* Avete esperienza lavorativa di 2-7 anni in un campo affine al settore ferroviario.
* Avete svolto una comprovata esperienza in ambito della gestione di Progetto (Project Management) e avete esperienza nella Supply Chain.
* Hai concluso una formazione in ambito tecnico ETH/ EPFL - SUP/FH o formazione equivalente con adeguata esperienza.
* Avete una buona conoscenza dell'italiano e delle buone conoscenze del tedesco parlato e scritto (B2) e dell'inglese (B2).

Das kannst du bewegen.
* Du vertrittst die Interessen der Bauherrschaft in sämtlichen Projektphasen - von der strategischen Planung über Ausschreibung und Vergabe bis zur Realisierung und Inbetriebnahme.
* Du verantwortest die Erreichung der Projektziele hinsichtlich Kosten, Termine, Qualität, Sicherheit und Funktionalität.
* Du steuerst und koordinierst externe Planungsbüros, Unternehmer sowie Fachspezialisten und sorgst für eine effiziente Zusammenarbeit aller Beteiligten.
* Du stellst die Einhaltung von Normen, Richtlinien, gesetzlichen Vorgaben und bauherrenseitigen Anforderungen sicher.
* Du führst ein transparentes Vertrags-, Nachtrags- und Claim-Management und identifizierst Chancen und Risiken frühzeitig, um geeignete Massnahmen zur erfolgreichen Projektsteuerung einzuleiten.
* Du agierst als zentrale Schnittstelle zwischen Bauherrschaft, Projektteams, Behörden, Betreiberorganisationen und weiteren Stakeholdern.
Das bringst du mit.
* Teamarbeit ist für dich die Grundlage erfolgreicher Projekte und du arbeitest gerne interdisziplinär.
* Du verfügst über ausgeprägte analytische, konzeptionelle und organisatorische Fähigkeiten sowie unternehmerisches Denken. Du handelst eigenverantwortlich, strukturiert und lösungsorientiert und überzeugst durch deine Kommunikationsstärke sowie dein Durchsetzungsvermögen.
* Du bringst mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Projektleitung, Projektsteuerung oder Bauherrenvertretung von Elektro-, Energie- oder gebäudetechnischen Anlagen mit.
* Kenntnisse im öffentlichen Beschaffungswesen sowie im Vertrags- und Nachtragsmanagement sind von Vorteil. Die Leistungs- und Vertragsmodelle der SIA sowie die relevanten Normen und Richtlinien im Bereich Elektro- und Infrastrukturanlagen sind dir vertrau.
* Du verfügst über einen Hochschulabschluss (FH/ETH/Universität) oder eine höhere Berufsbildung (HF, eidg. Fachausweis oder eidg. Diplom) im Bereich Elektrotechnik, Energieversorgung oder Gebäudetechnik.
* Du kommunizierst stilsicher auf Deutsch; Kenntnisse einer weiteren Landessprache sind von Vorteil.

Internally Titled People Program Manager (Assignment: Principal Analyst, Workday HCM)
At WelbeHealth, we serve our communities’ most vulnerable seniors through shared intention, pioneering spirit, and the courage to love. These core values and our participant-focus lead the way no matter what.
The Program Manager (Assignment: Principal Analyst, Workday HCM) is the core technical support resource for WelbeHealth’s Workday implementation and will play a critical role in delivery, starting with Phase 1 targeted for 2027.

Reporting to the Director, People Technology Transformation, this role will provide hands-on configuration expertise across Workday HCM modules, helping translate business needs into scalable and effective system solutions.

In addition to serving as a technical expert, this role will act as a thought partner on process design and system decision-making, while also helping train incoming Workday analysts and improve existing HRIS resources with experience outside of Workday.
This role is different because the Program Manager (Assignment: Principal Analyst, Workday HCM) at WelbeHealth:
Serves as the organization's hands-on Workday HCM technical expert, partnering with business and technology leaders to design, configure, and optimize Workday solutions that support scalable People processes, regulatory compliance, and team member experience
Plays a foundational role in the successful delivery of WelbeHealth's enterprise Workday implementation by translating complex business requirements into effective system configurations, guiding technical decision-making, mentoring future Workday analysts, and helping build long-term internal Workday expertise

s.h: We care about our team members. That’s why we offer
s.t:
Medical insurance coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)
Work/life balance - We mean it! 17 days of personal time off (PTO), 12 holidays observed annually, and 6 sick days
401K savings + match

Serve as the primary hands-on Workday HCM configuration resource of the implementation across payroll, absence, time keeping, recruiting, HCM, performance and talent optimization, Peakon, benefits and Cloud Connect, and LMS
Partner with the Director, People Technology Reimagination, the People Project Manager, and key stakeholders to gather requirements, translate business needs, and recommend effective Workday configuration decisions aligned to future-state processes
Configure Workday HCM modules and related functionality to support business requirements, compliance needs, reporting needs, and team member experience
Support solution design sessions by identifying configuration options, implications, dependencies, and tradeoffs, serving as both a technical expert and thought partner for how people processes should be enabled in Workday
Partner in testing activities across unit, integration, and user acceptance testing by preparing configuration for test cycles, validating outcomes, supporting defect resolution, and helping ensure readiness for launch
Document configuration decisions, business process design, assumptions, dependencies, and technical considerations to support knowledge transfer, auditability, and ongoing support
Partner closely with internal teams and implementation partners to troubleshoot issues, evaluate impacts, and support resolution of system and process questions throughout the implementation lifecycle, as well as serve as a mentor for incoming Workday analysts to help upskill existing HRIS resources with prior experience outside of Workday to build internal capability and long-term support capacity

Bachelor’s degree in human resources, information systems, business, or related field preferred; equivalent Workday configuration experience may be substituted
Required hands-on Workday HCM configuration experience, with depth across as many modules as possible including HCM, payroll, absence, time keeping, recruiting, performance and talent optimization, Peakon, benefits and Cloud Connect, and LMS
Demonstrated ability translating business requirements into effective Workday configuration solutions and providing thoughtful recommendations on how processes should be designed and enabled in the system
Experience supporting Workday implementations through design, configuration, testing, defect resolution, and launch activities
Strong technical aptitude with the ability to evaluate dependencies, troubleshoot issues, document solutions, and maintain a high level of detail and accuracy
Ability to serve as a trainer, mentor, and knowledge resource for incoming Workday analysts and existing HRIS team members transitioning from other systems
Collaborative working style with the ability to partner effectively with project management, business stakeholders, IT, vendors, and implementation partners
We are seeking a Program Manager who is passionate about leveraging technology to transform the employee experience in a mission-driven healthcare environment.

The ideal candidate brings deep hands-on Workday HCM configuration expertise, strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and the ability to partner with cross-functional stakeholders to design scalable, future-focused solutions.

If you're looking for an opportunity to play a key technical leadership role in one of the organization's most strategic People technology initiatives while helping build lasting internal Workday capability, we'd love to hear from you.
Compensation consists of base salary plus bonus. WelbeHealth offers a competitive total rewards package that includes a 401(k) match, comprehensive healthcare coverage, and a broad range of additional benefits. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience and relevant qualifications.

Führe dein Team in eine erfolgreiche Zukunft! Du übernimmst die Leitung der Geschäftsstelle, steuerst Projekte und Finanzen, pflegst enge Kundenbeziehungen und entwickelst das Geschäftsfeld weiter.
Leiter/in Geschäftsstelle Elektro Stadt Luzern (w/m/d)
Pensum: 80% \- 100%
Das kannst du gestalten
Du führst ein engagiertes Team von rund 20 Mitarbeitenden inklusive Lernende und förderst mit Weitblick, Teamgeist und technischer Kompetenz ein nachhaltiges Wachstum.
Du gewinnst neue Aufträge, betreust deine Kundschaft persönlich und planst sowie realisierst Elektroinstallationen.
Du förderst dein Team in fachlicher, methodischer und sozialer Hinsicht und begleitest die Ausbildung von Lernenden engagiert und als Vorbild.
Du überwachst Geschäftsergebnisse und Projektverläufe und leitest bei Bedarf gezielt wirkungsvolle Massnahmen ein.
Du hältst dein Wissen in zukunftsorientierten Bereichen wie E\-Mobilität und Photovoltaik durch deine Teilnahme an internen Schulungen kontinuierlich aktuell.
Du nutzt dein regionales Netzwerk, erkennst Marktpotenziale und bringst deine Ideen aktiv in die Weiterentwicklung des Geschäfts ein.
Das macht dich aus·
Du hast eine abgeschlossene Grundausbildung im Bereich der Elektroinstallation mit EFZ und bringst die Meisterprüfung mit \- oder befindest dich auf dem Weg dorthin.
Du bringst fundierte Erfahrung mit Stark\- und Schwachstrominstallationen sowie solides Wissen zu Normen und Vorschriften mit.
Du bist eine motivierende Persönlichkeit, übernimmst Verantwortung und gibst dein Know\-how gerne weiter.
Du förderst eine gesunde Teamkultur, gehst achtsam mit deinen Ressourcen um und unterstützt andere dabei.
Du bist in der Region verankert und engagierst dich gerne auch über das Berufliche hinaus.
Das macht uns aus
Ein spannender Job. Eine sinnstiftende Arbeit. Und dann noch zahlreiche weitere Vorteile, die dir CKW bietet.
? Attraktive Vergütung und umfangreiche Sozialleistungen: Freue dich auf faire Bezahlung und umfassende Vorsorgepakete, die deine Zukunft absichern.
? Beruf und Privatleben im Einklang: Mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten, Teilzeitmodellen und bis zu 50% Home\-Office (je nach Tätigkeit) ermöglichen wir eine gesunde Balance zwischen Arbeit und Privatleben.
? Talentförderung: Dein persönliches und berufliches Wachstum liegt uns am Herzen. Wir unterstützen dich bei Aus\- oder Weiterbildungen.
? Attraktive Extras: Profitiere von unseren Angeboten wie vergünstigten Mobile\-Abos, Unterstützung bei der Kinderbetreuung, Ferienkauf oder kostenlosen Parkplätzen. Mehr erfahren
Bei CKW setzen wir uns für eine Kultur der Nichtdiskriminierung, Toleranz und Inklusion ein. Als Arbeitgeberin, der Chancengleichheit wichtig ist, begrüßen wir Bewerbungen unabhängig von Herkunft, Geschlechtsidentität und \-ausdruck, sexueller Orientierung, Alter, Behinderung sowie sozialem, kulturellem und religiösem Hintergrund. Wir engagieren uns für einen respektvollen und inklusiven Bewerbungsprozess und Arbeitsplatz für alle.

A major function of the Office of Data Acquisitions is to provide databases developed from state highway safety related data for use in analyses aimed at reducing deaths, injuries, crashes, and medical costs.

As the Director, the incumbent will be responsible for the following: Advising the Associate Administrator on all matters related to the design, development, coordination, and management of crash investigation and data collection, and their contribution to achieving the mission of NHTSA.

Keeps the Associate Administrator fully informed as to the status of programs and of problems and controversial issues.

Collaborates closely with the Associate Administrator and other top officials of NHTSA to identify the agency's crash research and data needs, to determine techniques and methods by which the office can meet those needs, to estimate the cost and time required to meet the needs, and to determine other implications of changes.

Carrying out personnel management responsibilities for a staff of professional, technical, administrative and clerical support personnel. Makes decisions on work problems presented by subordinate supervisors and key specialists.

Evaluates performance of subordinate supervisors and reviews evaluations made by supervisors of subordinate employee's performance. Establishing policy and provides management oversight of the State Data Reporting Systems Division responsible for the crash record-based data.

Crash record based data includes the Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS), a fundamental national data base on traffic safety, Crash Report Sampling System (CRSS), Not-in-Traffic System (NTS) and the State Electronic Data Collection Program (SEDC)., The Division also provides the expertise in sample design and quality control to the other offices in the National Center for Statistics and Analysis, the rest of NHTSA and other offices in DOT.

Establishing policy and provides management oversight of the Crash Investigation Division (CID), provides executive leadership in the planning, design, development, coordination, and management of national networks of motor vehicle traffic crash research and data collection activities.

These include the operation of a national system to conduct detailed investigations of a well-defined selection of motor vehicle crashes currently the Crash Investigation Sampling System (CISS)); and the Special Crash Investigations (SCI) program of special investigations of crashes of particular, interest; and Systems for collecting, supplementing, and coding data from police crash reports to provide special purpose data files.

Maintaining liaison with other Federal agencies, State and local governments, police agencies, hospitals, private safety groups, motor vehicle and equipment manufacturers, crash research and analysis organizations, professional societies, and other groups with an interest in crash investigation and crash data for the purposes are for exchanging crash data and information on crash research technology, encouraging the use of crash data, and cooperating on crash research programs.

The ideal candidate is a data executive and systems expert with a track record of managing federal data collection, automation, and national crash investigation programs.

They possess the strategic and technical skills to lead multi-disciplinary teams while directing the human resource, budgetary, and procurement parameters vital to national highway safety initiatives.

A skilled collaborator, they excel at building partnerships across federal, state, and private sectors including law enforcement, public health, and the automotive industry to secure cooperation and advance data systems.

Furthermore, they bring expertise in data governance, enforcing quality control and data completeness while protecting individual privacy, ensuring the delivery of accurate databases that support national safety research and rulemaking.
To meet the minimum qualifications for this position, you must meet the specialized experience qualifications.

To qualify for the Grade 15, you must have at least one year of specialized experience equal or equivalent to the GS-14, it must include: Experience directing multi-disciplinary professional, technical, and administrative teams while managing the organizational, human resource, and budgetary parameters vital to national highway traffic safety initiatives.

Experience communicating with system managers, rulemaking engineers, researchers, technicians, traffic safety administrators, Governor's Representatives for Highway Safety, State and local officials, national data system program managers and others associated with the application of data as it applies to helping solve complex safety issues.

Experience establishing policy and overseeing large federal data divisions to ensure data completeness, security, and rigorous quality control. Examples include working with executive leadership to plan, develop, and manage large-scale national data collection systems and multi-level crash investigation programs.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Technical Knowledge: Knowledge of federal budgeting to manage large divisional funds, appropriations, large-scale national data architecture, data collection methodologies, complex procurement or contracting mechanisms and systems engineering principles required to build and sustain nationwide databases.

Leadership and Supervision: Management and/or team leader skills, including the ability to direct, manage, and develop a diverse, high-performing human resources workforce of technical and administrative staff.

Communication: Communication, presentation, and negotiation skills, including the ability to secure community support, build strategic intergovernmental alliances, and establish private-sector data-sharing partnerships.

Reasoning: Ability to collaborate across federal, state, and private boundaries to improve data accessibility while balancing competing stakeholder priorities.

For all types of consideration, experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

The Data Center Security Risk & Assurance Senior Program Manager drives the maturity and execution of CoreWeave’s data center physical security controls compliance program.

Reporting to the Senior Manager, Data Center Risk and Assurance, this role ensures that all Data Center Security designs, controls, and operational practices tied to the company’s audit and customer requirements across CoreWeave’s global data center footprint meet defined security standards, regulatory requirements, and organizational expectations.

This role will also support new site selection, physical security due diligence, and initial risk evaluation for the EMEA region.
This Program Manager will own the Data Center Security-specific audit framework, oversee comprehensive risk and assurance audits within our operations sites, and partner closely with Security Design, Operations, Legal, and Engineering teams to validate adherence to CoreWeave and its partners’ security objectives.

The role requires a strategic thinker with an understanding of physical and operational audit scope, an eye for control assurance, scalability, and strong cross-functional influence in a fast-growing, high-performance environment.

Represent CoreWeave’s Data Center Security Operations team, ensuring all DC Security controls and processes align with internal standards, customer contractual requirements, and external regulatory frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, NIST, etc.).
Audit & Assessments: Plan and lead independent internal audits and control validations across CoreWeave’s data center network; deliver actionable findings and track remediation, ensuring timely treatment.
Operational Assurance: Partner with Data Center Operations, Security Design, Security Operations, and Technical Program Management teams to verify that physical security controls are implemented, maintained, and effective.
Site Selection Due Diligence: Conduct physical security due diligence for site selection, ensuring appropriate security requirements are included in Master Service Agreements and other lease contracts, collaborating with Site Selection and Legal teams.
Post Lease or Build Contract Execution: This role informs and collaborates with the Security Design and Security Operations teams to communicate site security requirements.
Metrics and Reporting: Ensure assessments and audit evidence are managed and reported in accordance with CoreWeave controls compliance mechanisms to track control health, audit outcomes, and risk trends.
Collaboration & Influence: Build strong relationships with internal partners, fostering a culture of accountability and proactive risk management throughout the data center lifecycle.
Emerging Risk Monitoring: Stay current with evolving threat landscapes, compliance standards, and industry best practices to ensure CoreWeave’s data center security programs remain resilient and forward-looking.

5+ years of experience in security risk management, compliance, or assurance functions, ideally within cloud, hyperscale, or critical infrastructure environments.
Proven success leading risk audits and assurance programs in complex, high-growth organizations.
Strong understanding of physical and logical security controls, risk frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO 27001, ISO22237, ISO22301, SOC 2, HITrust, FedRAMP), and data center operational security.
Demonstrated ability to translate technical security concepts into actionable business insights and governance structures.
Excellent communication, influencing, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
Relevant certifications or on-the-job experience (CISSP, CISM, CRISC, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor) preferred.

Gedeihen Sie in einem dynamischen Umfeld, in dem kein Tag wie der andere ist - mal begrüssen Sie eine internationale Führungskraft, mal koordinieren Sie eine reibungslos ablaufende Konferenz? Dann ist dies Ihre Bühne.
** **
### **Stellenübersicht** ###
Als Event & Guest Experience Manager sind Sie verantwortlich für die professionelle Betreuung unserer internationalen Gäste sowie die Planung, Organisation und Durchführung von Veranstaltungen. Sie begleiten den gesamten Guest Journey Prozess von der Ankunft bis zur Abreise und sorgen gleichzeitig für eine reibungslose Umsetzung von Events und Konferenzdienstleistungen.
Als Gastgeber/in und Event Profi sind Sie eine wichtige Visitenkarte des Centre of Global Dialogue. Mit Ihrer hohen Serviceorientierung, Ihrem Organisationstalent und Ihrem Engagement schaffen Sie erstklassige Erlebnisse für Gäste, Kunden und Veranstaltungsteilnehmende.
Die Rolle ist Teil einer integrierten Event & Guest Experience Organisation mit dem Ziel, dass Mitarbeitende flexibel in beiden Bereichen eingesetzt werden und sich gegenseitig vertreten. Alle Mitarbeitenden übernehmen sowohl Empfangs- als auch Konferenz- und Eventmanagement-Aufgaben, um maximale Flexibilität, gegenseitige Vertretung und ein herausragendes Gästeerlebnis sicherzustellen.
** **
**Ihre Aufgaben**
**Guest Experience & Reception**
* Empfang, Betreuung und Beratung von internationalen Gästen, Besuchern und Veranstaltungsteilnehmenden in Deutsch und Englisch.
* Sicherstellung einer professionellen und herzlichen Gästeerfahrung als erste Ansprechperson des Unternehmens sowie Verantwortung für die Reservation der Hotelzimmer im Centre of Global Dialogue.
* Sicherstellung eines reibungslosen Tagesgeschäfts am Empfang sowie Betreuung des Visitor Management Systems und der Besucherregistrierung, Check In und Check Out
* Flexible Übernahme von Empfangs-, Reservations- und Gästeserviceaufgaben im Rahmen eines bereichsübergreifenden Einsatzmodells, als einheitlicher Prozess mit den Eventaufgaben.
** **
**Conference & Event Management**
* Planung und Organisation sowie Durchführung von internen Veranstaltungen.
* Koordination aller relevanten Eventdienstleistungen wie Raumplanung, Unterkunft, Verpflegung, Technik und Logistik.
* Bearbeitung des Entrygates für unsere Neuanfragen
* Unterstützung der Gäste und Seminarteilnehmenden bei administrativen Anliegen sowie Vermittlung an interne Schnittstellen.
** **
**Fachliche Kompetenzen**
* Ausgeprägte Dienstleistungs- und Kundenorientierung.
* Starke organisatorische Fähigkeiten und hohe Eigenverantwortung.
* Fähigkeit, mehrere Aufgaben gleichzeitig zu koordinieren und Prioritäten richtig zu setzen.
* Strukturierte, lösungsorientierte und selbstständige Arbeitsweise.
* Erfahrung mit Planet (Protel), Momentus (Ungerboeck), Visitor Registration Tools oder vergleichbaren Systemen von Vorteil.
** **
### **Über das Team** ###
Das Event Management Team von Swiss Re ist Teil von **Corporate Real Estate & Services (CRES) Zürich** und plant und realisiert ein breites Spektrum an Veranstaltungen für interne und externe Kunden im gesamten Unternehmen.

Das Team hält sich an Swiss Re's hohe Qualitätsstandards und sorgt dafür, dass jede Veranstaltung unsere Marke und unsere Werte widerspiegelt.

In enger Zusammenarbeit mit verschiedenen Geschäftsbereichen und einem etablierten Lieferantennetzwerk agiert das Team mit Präzision, Kreativität und einem ausgeprägten Servicebewusstsein - und macht jede Veranstaltung zu einem Erlebnis, das in Erinnerung bleibt.
### **Über Sie** ###
Sie sind eine geborene Gastgeberperson - jemand, der echte Freude daran findet, andere willkommen zu heissen, ihnen das Gefühl zu geben, geschätzt und gut betreut zu werden. Sie bringen Energie und Ruhe in gleichem Masse mit, bleiben gelassen, wenn es hektisch wird, und finden Lösungen, bevor Probleme entstehen.

Sie kommunizieren sicher und herzlich über Kulturen und Hierarchien hinweg und sind stolz auf die Qualität Ihrer Arbeit. Sie schätzen Abwechslung, passen sich schnell an und arbeiten gerne in einem kollegialen Team, in dem alle füreinander da sind.
** **
**Sie sind**
* Gastgeber/in aus Leidenschaft und schaffen außergewöhnliche Gästeerlebnisse.
* Service-, kunden- und lösungsorientiert, gleichzeitig positiv, engagiert und teamorientiert.
* Belastbar, flexibel und behalten auch in hektischen Situationen den Überblick.
* Kommunikativ, professionell und souverän im Umgang mit unterschiedlichen Anspruchsgruppen in Deutsch und Englisch.
* Zuverlässig, qualitätsbewusst, verantwortungsvoll, diskret und loyal.
* Aufgeschlossen gegenüber flexiblen Arbeitszeitmodellen und einer engen teamübergreifenden Zusammenarbeit.
* Freude an einer vielseitigen Tätigkeit mit wechselnden Schwerpunkten zwischen Reception, Hospitality und Event Management.

* Arbeitsort: Swiss Re Centre for Global Dialogue in Rüschlikon, hybrides Arbeiten nach Absprache
* Arbeitszeiten: Montag bis Freitag zwischen 06:30 und 20:00Uhr gem. Einsatzplanung, gelegentlich Wochenendeinsätze
